name: The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery
summary: Coordinates coding agents through typed hypothesis contracts, sandboxed experiments, shared memory, retrospective ablations, and evidence-linked manuscript audits. Evaluation includes 70 computational ML campaigns scored by an AI-reviewer proxy and separate held-out case studies. Its single accepted ALIFE paper involved substantial human specification, verification, statistical analysis, and editing; automated rubric gates also missed evaluation-protocol changes.

name: ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence
summary: Links literature notes, code-search artifacts, and manuscript claims through a Chain-of-Evidence workflow and four-part integrity audit. In 75 adapted ADRS runs, it reports strong score reproduction and reference identity checks, with human correction of flagged audit results. Majority-vote checks still miss documented exploits; MLE-bench medal results use repeated test-grader feedback rather than the official single-submission protocol.

name: ScientistTwo: Pioneering the Human Knowledge Frontier with Autonomous AI
summary: Coordinates limitation-driven hypotheses, subset-to-full experiments, ablation-based refinement, and simulated review–rebuttal cycles that can trigger supplementary experiments. Across 107 selected ML-paper challenges, it reports 86 successful improvements; gains and most review scores condition on those successes. Acceptance figures come from automated reviewers, with a 33-paper human assessment; reported cost averages about $3,765 per completed NeurIPS-derived task.

name: ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents
summary: Provides a biomedical workspace that couples instruction/skill-harness revision with model reinforcement learning. Case studies report fixed-model adaptation, fixed-harness pass@4 gains, and three alternating update cycles on scientific QA tasks. Real researcher interactions illustrate task and rubric construction; the controlled adaptation experiment uses bounded simulated feedback, and individual feedback or skill contributions are not isolated.

name: The AI Scientist: Towards Fully Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery
summary: Uses human-prepared ML experiment templates, literature-assisted ideation, Aider code edits, experiment logs, and LaTeX generation to produce papers and automated reviews. Three small computational task families show substantial execution and writing attrition; reported acceptance thresholds come from its own reviewer. The paper documents metric errors, implementation mistakes, data leakage, hallucinated details, and unsafe execution behavior requiring human checks.

name: The AI Scientist-v2: Workshop-Level Automated Scientific Discovery via Agentic Tree Search
summary: Replaces code templates with staged agentic tree search, replication nodes, and visual feedback for experiments and manuscripts. Humans selected three ideas and the best outputs from multiple autonomous runs for workshop review; one passed and was withdrawn as agreed. Internal audits document train/test overlap, misdescribed methods, and claimed experiments absent from successful code, so acceptance is bounded evidence of workshop-level manuscript quality.

name: AI-Researcher: Autonomous Scientific Innovation
summary: Combines literature/code analysis, concept-to-implementation mapping, iterative advisor-guided experiments, and hierarchical manuscript drafting. Scientist-Bench evaluates guided and reference-only ML research tasks using execution checks and LLM rubric/pairwise judgments. Reported completion differs from correctness, reviewer preferences vary substantially, and benchmark prompts can expose target-method details; the study does not independently establish human-level scientific quality.

name: Agent Laboratory: Using LLM Agents as Research Assistants
summary: Assists a human-supplied research idea through literature review, iterative ML coding, and report drafting, with optional feedback checkpoints. Small human studies find useful outputs but substantially lower paper-quality scores than automated reviewers; co-pilot gains concentrate in quality and presentation. Separate MLE-bench tests evaluate the solver component, while reported cost savings compare different workflow settings rather than matched scientific outcomes.

name: AgentRxiv: Towards Collaborative Autonomous Research
summary: Adds a searchable shared report archive to Agent Laboratory so sequential or parallel research agents can reuse earlier findings. Prompting-search experiments improve best-so-far MATH-500 accuracy and show mixed transfer to other QA benchmarks. The target test set guides repeated search, parallel runs use more resources, and humans manually verify code and outputs because agents can fabricate results or remove essential method logic.

name: Denario Project: Deep Knowledge Artificial Intelligence Agents for Scientific Discovery
summary: Provides modular agents for ideation, literature checks, analysis, code execution, and paper drafting across supplied scientific datasets. Its journal tutorial evaluates heterogeneous drafts through team expert self-assessment, with substantial prompt and verification roles for humans. Outputs require expert development; documented failures include silent synthetic-data substitution, unsupported citations, missing solvers and invented results. The interdisciplinary demonstration is a single case.

name: Kosmos: An AI Scientist for Autonomous Discovery
summary: Coordinates parallel literature and data-analysis agents through a structured world model to produce source-linked discovery reports from human-curated datasets. Seven case studies include reproduced findings and new hypotheses, with human reanalysis and external validation. Experts supported79.4% of102 sampled statements, with lower interpretation accuracy; reported months of saved work are collaborator estimates, and one final discovery report involved manual curation.

name: Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist
summary: Google’s Gemini-based Co-Scientist generates, critiques and evolves research hypotheses through literature search and Elo-ranked agent debates. Expert-guided evaluations include selected AML drug and combination assays, liver-organoid tests and rediscovery of unpublished antimicrobial-resistance findings. Human screening and laboratory work remain central; several candidates failed, biological effects were context dependent, and automated Elo scores do not establish general scientific correctness.

name: SciAgents: Automating Scientific Discovery Through Bioinspired Multi-Agent Intelligent Graph Reasoning
summary: SciAgents uses knowledge-graph paths and specialized LLM agents to generate, expand and critique biologically inspired materials proposals. A literature-search assistant assigns novelty and feasibility scores to illustrative examples. Reported mechanical, optical and energy improvements are predictions; the study does not synthesize materials, execute the proposed simulations or independently establish superiority over human research.
status: Journal publication verified in Advanced Materials 37, article 2413523 (2025), first published online on 18 December 2024. The displayed date remains the 9 September 2024 first preprint. Publication status does not establish experimental realization of the proposed materials.

name: SciMON: Scientific Inspiration Machines Optimized for Novelty
summary: SciMON retrieves semantic, graph and citation-based inspirations to generate scientific idea sentences, then revises suggestions that resemble prior work. Expert studies find improvements over baseline models, but NLP ideas remain substantially less novel and technically detailed than source papers. Evaluations use extracted problem contexts and seed terms; novelty gains are conditional on selected revisions, without executing the proposed research.

name: ResearchAgent: Iterative Research Idea Generation over Scientific Literature with Large Language Models
summary: ResearchAgent combines citation-linked paper abstracts, retrieved entities and LLM reviewers to draft and iteratively refine research problems, methods and experiment plans. Human and model evaluations favour the full GPT-4 system over simpler variants, while weaker backbones benefit inconsistently. Evidence concerns proposal ratings; the system does not execute experiments, and entity-linking noise and reviewer agreement limit claims of scientific validity.

name: MOOSE-Chem: Large Language Models for Rediscovering Unseen Chemistry Scientific Hypotheses
summary: MOOSE-Chem retrieves paper inspirations and evolves chemistry hypotheses through LLM mutation, critique and recombination. On 51 retrospectively decomposed papers it recovers parts of known innovations, but evaluation seeds the literature corpus with the true inspirations and selects candidates using answer-aware similarity scores. Expert ratings are lower than automatic scores, ranking remains weak, and proposed chemistry is not experimentally validated.

name: Coscientist: Autonomous chemical research with large language models
summary: Coscientist connects GPT-4 planning, web and documentation search, code execution and laboratory APIs. It executes known coupling reactions and bounded instrument tasks, with researcher-prepared resources, manual plate movement and occasional guidance. Reaction-optimization results use previously collected datasets rather than a live laboratory loop. Only a simplified implementation is released, and the demonstrations do not establish autonomous novel chemical discovery.

name: ChemCrow: Augmenting large language models with chemistry tools
summary: ChemCrow equips GPT-4 with chemistry tools for retrieval, molecular analysis, synthesis planning and robotic execution. It synthesized four known compounds and helped a human-guided workflow identify a new chromophore, whose absorption differed by 33 nm from the target. Expert evaluations favour factuality over tool-free GPT-4, but reasoning failures persist; laboratory oversight and proprietary services remain necessary, and the public release includes only 12 of 18 tools.

name: The Virtual Lab of AI agents designs new SARS-CoV-2 nanobodies
summary: Organizes a principal-investigator agent and scientific specialists into meetings with high-level human guidance. The agents develop a computational nanobody-design workflow, with selected designs tested experimentally. This demonstrates a specific human-AI research collaboration; human laboratory work and biological validation are central parts of the evidence.

name: Biomni: A General-Purpose Biomedical AI Agent
summary: Combines retrieval-guided planning and executable code with an environment of biomedical tools, software, and databases. Evaluations span heterogeneous tasks, multimodal data analysis, and experimental protocol design. The reported breadth supports biomedical research assistance; benchmark performance and protocol case studies should not be treated as general clinical validation.

name: BioDiscoveryAgent: An AI Agent for Designing Genetic Perturbation Experiments
summary: Uses an LLM to select genetic perturbation batches, incorporate observed phenotypes, and optionally retrieve literature, search gene databases, or critique selections. Retrospective replay across six single-gene screens and one paired-gene screen measures hit discovery against optimization and random baselines. Gains depend on dataset, model, and budget; added tools can hurt stronger models, and the study does not establish prospective autonomous biological discovery.

name: Robin: A multi-agent system for automating scientific discovery
summary: Combines literature retrieval, LLM-ranked therapeutic hypotheses and notebook data-analysis agents in a human-run experimental loop. The Nature study reports phagocytosis-enhancing candidates in cultured retinal cells, including primary cells from one donor. Experts supply protocols, physical experiments, preprocessing and analysis prompts; these in-vitro findings do not establish clinical effectiveness, and broad productivity gains are estimated rather than measured against a human research team.

name: FunSearch: Mathematical discoveries from program search with large language models
summary: Pairs a language model with an evaluator and an evolving database of programs, searching for code that constructs strong solutions. The paper reports new cap-set constructions and improved bin-packing heuristics. Its successes depend on explicit evaluators and problem specifications, making the verification mechanism central to its scientific relevance.

name: AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery
summary: Evolves candidate programs using language-model edits and feedback from executable evaluators. Applications include mathematical constructions, algorithm discovery, and infrastructure optimization. The white paper illustrates breadth when a reliable scoring procedure exists; reported improvements are tied to those tasks and do not imply autonomous formulation of every scientific objective.

name: EvoScientist: Towards Multi-Agent Evolving AI Scientists for End-to-End Scientific Discovery
summary: Coordinates a researcher, engineer and evolution manager that turn prior idea reviews and execution trajectories into retrievable ideation and experimentation memories. On 30 curated AI queries, it reports stronger judged ideas and higher mean code-execution success after memory updates. Human comparisons cover four baselines; selected conference-track acceptances are case evidence, and execution success does not establish scientific correctness or cross-domain autonomous discovery.

name: From AI for Science to Agentic Science: A Survey on Autonomous Scientific Discovery
summary: Organizes agentic science across life sciences, chemistry, materials, and physics, connecting capability, workflow, and domain perspectives. It provides a useful map of hypothesis generation, experimentation, analysis, and refinement. As a survey, its taxonomy helps navigate reported systems rather than independently reproducing their discovery or autonomy claims.

name: A Survey of AI Scientists
summary: Synthesizes AI-scientist systems through six stages covering literature, ideas, preparation, execution, writing, and paper generation. The revised survey traces the shift from individual components to integrated workflows and discusses robustness and governance. Its stage-based organization is useful for comparing coverage, but does not make unlike evaluation settings directly comparable.

name: Autonomous Research Agents: A Survey of AI Scientists and the Verification Gap
summary: Examines computational research agents through autonomy, evaluation, released artifacts, human intervention, novelty checks, and result-selection disclosure. Its coded corpus distinguishes runnable code from evidence that supports scientific claims. The conclusions are bounded by the screened AI/ML systems and coding rules, rather than a census of all scientific domains.

name: Can AI Scientists Coordinate at Runtime?
summary: Lets current agents choose authorized host capabilities at runtime, with optional scoped contracts and advisory artifact checks. A single-seed study of three hosts finds the highest ResearchClawBench means with runtime selection alone; contracts plus verification reduce those means. Verification does not block transitions, budget matching is not fully reconciled, and an exploratory DiscoveryBench subset gives different rankings.

name: MOOSE-Star: Unlocking Tractable Training for Scientific Discovery by Breaking the Complexity Barrier
summary: Trains hypothesis generation through decomposed discovery subtasks, motivation-guided hierarchical retrieval, and bounded composition. TOMATO-Star supplies paper-derived supervision; evaluations measure retrieval and LLM-scored reconstruction of held-out hypotheses. The best-case complexity reduction relies on compositional and routing assumptions, and the study does not prospectively validate new discoveries.

name: MOOSE-Chem2: Exploring LLM Limits in Fine-Grained Scientific Hypothesis Discovery via Hierarchical Search
summary: Expands coarse research directions into increasingly detailed hypotheses through hierarchical search, comparing different language-model scoring ensembles. Evaluation uses expert-annotated fine-grained hypotheses from recent literature. The study tests alignment with known hypotheses and model-defined rewards; a detailed, high-scoring proposal still needs independent checks and experimental testing.

name: Scideator: Human-LLM Compound System for Scientific Ideation through Facet Recombination and Novelty Evaluation
summary: Extracts purpose, mechanism, and evaluation facets from papers so researchers can recombine ideas and inspect related work for novelty. A 22-person CS study reports greater perceived creativity support than a bundled baseline; separate ablations test retrieval and classification. Novelty confidence and several idea-quality ratings do not improve, and neither the study nor its retrieval-based labels validate completed scientific results.

name: CycleResearcher: Improving Automated Research via Automated Review
summary: Trains research-writing and reviewing models through supervised learning and iterative preference optimization. Main evaluations score manuscripts whose experimental results are deliberately fabricated, so simulated acceptance measures writing and reviewer alignment. Human reviewers rate selected outputs below typical submissions. A separate executed appendix example uses an external coding agent, but contains numerical and interpretation errors that limit claims of validated discovery.

name: The Automation of Science (Robot Scientist Adam)
summary: Combines hypothesis generation, automated laboratory experiments, and a logical record of the research process to study yeast functional genomics. The authors report manual confirmation of Adam's conclusions. This pre-LLM example grounds modern autonomy discussions in a closed experimental loop and explicit provenance within a constrained biological problem.

name: Autonomous LLM-driven research from data to human-verifiable research papers
summary: Guides agents from annotated data through hypotheses, analysis code, and manuscripts while linking numeric results back to producing code. Repeated case studies show fewer major errors for simple tasks, limited novelty, and failures on complex data or goals that require human review. The evaluated workflow includes prepared metadata and step approvals; traceability supports verification without establishing scientific correctness.

name: Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
summary: Compares expert-written NLP prompting proposals with selected agent-generated proposals in blinded reviews involving 104 researchers. AI proposals receive higher novelty ratings across several analyses; lower feasibility estimates are not statistically conclusive. Limited idea diversity, unreliable automatic ranking, and unfaithful execution-agent implementations constrain interpretation. The study measures perceived proposal quality rather than demonstrated scientific outcomes.

name: Empirical Research Assistance: An AI system to help scientists write expert-level empirical software
summary: Uses LLM code rewriting and tree search to improve supplied scientific evaluation metrics, incorporating expert guidance, paper summaries, and recombined ideas. Experiments report gains in single-cell integration, retrospective forecasting, and other computational tasks. Results depend on task-specific scoring and data splits; forecasting comparisons use dated retrospective data, and implementation audits disclose failures and departures from some proposed methods.

name: Towards end-to-end automation of AI research
summary: Combines template-based and template-free agents for research ideas, experiments, manuscripts, and automated review. The Nature paper consolidates earlier AI Scientist reports and adds analyses; its workshop campaign overlaps v2. One selected manuscript received acceptance-level reviews before withdrawal. Human selection, code and data errors, and model-based evaluation constrain claims of independent scientific validation.

name: The Ideation-Execution Gap: Execution Outcomes of LLM-Generated versus Human Research Ideas
summary: Recruits researchers to execute randomly assigned human- or model-generated NLP ideas, then obtains blinded reviews of the resulting projects. AI proposals show larger declines from ideation ratings, but final project-level differences are not statistically conclusive. Attrition, implementation changes, and differences between review stages qualify interpretation; the study demonstrates why proposal ratings alone are weak proxies for completed research quality.
status: ICLR 2026 publication identity verified. The displayed date remains the first preprint; version-comparison limits are recorded in the full-text notes.

name: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
summary: Extracts atomic claims from published cancer-registry studies, executes reproduction analyses, and tests alternative analytical choices through agent-generated perturbations. SEER-Repro supplies the evaluation setting. The authors distinguish reproducing reported findings from assessing their sensitivity; flagged alternatives require expert review, and report-based grading does not independently verify the complete analysis code.

name: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses
summary: Develops hypothesis trees through multi-agent search, converts selected plans into Harbor tasks, and uses contribution-weighted offline model training and fixed-model workflow replay for later runs. DFM-Bench scores proposals and research histories. Automated investigation-design gains coexist with declining novelty and importance; retrospective publication correspondence is sensitive to retrieval and group differences. Compiled plans do not establish completed, independently validated discoveries.
status: Summary follows v2, revised 20 October 2026; date records the first submission on 16 October.

name: Automating ML for Science: Can Frontier Agents Climb Scientific Hills in the Wild?
summary: Studies frontier coding agents improving scientific ML baselines in Agent4Sci, separating optimization, held-out evaluation, and trajectory auditing. Default gains are largely engineering-driven; targeted research skills produce more varied interventions. The study distinguishes metric improvement from scientific insight, with limitations from run variance, imperfect audits, task-specific skills, and the absence of a human-researcher baseline.
status: The arXiv comment names the NeurIPS 2026 E&D Track; a proceedings record was not verified, so the source label remains preprint.

name: RIDAR: Safeguarding Research Integrity in Autonomous Research Agents via Automated Detection and Runtime Intervention
summary: Audits research trajectories with separate Analyzer and Verifier agents, then tests runtime feedback against matched unassisted runs. Its taxonomy covers 14 integrity violations. Reported findings depend on LLM judgments and mathematics/ML tasks; testing files and extra resources remain accessible deliberately, so detected violation rates should not be generalized to environments enforcing those boundaries.
status: Annotation follows the October arXiv preprint. An earlier ICLR 2027 submission was withdrawn; its title and reported results differ.

name: SoundnessBench: Can Your AI Scientist Really Tell Good Research Ideas from Bad Ones?
summary: Examines whether language models can assess methodological soundness before experiments are run. Results-masked proposals receive reviewer-derived proxy labels and separate expert judgments on a subset. Standard prompts favor approval, while aggressive prompts trade false approvals for false rejections. The study concerns proposal-stage judgment; its labels do not establish experimental truth or general research quality.
status: Reviewed v3, revised 23 October 2026; date retains the first arXiv submission on 28 May.

name: ADAPT for Science: A Multi-Agent System for Self-Evolving Scientific Optimization
summary: Combines retrieval of historical scientific designs, evolving start-selection strategies, and optimizer-program evolution under physical constraints. The authors evaluate gravitational-wave detector designs on eight held-out topologies using a differentiable simulator and matched scientific evaluation budgets. Results support optimization within this setting; transfer beyond simulation and dependence on historical-library coverage remain open.

name: GeoAgent: Contract-Constrained LLM Agents for Seismic Data Processing
summary: Connects seismic-processing tools through a fixed nine-stage graph, with explicit contracts for artifacts, input resolution, parameter ownership, and output validation. Deterministic geometry checks address failures that prompting alone did not prevent. Evidence comes from engineering measurements on one dataset and model family; adaptive planning, migration quality, and broader controlled comparisons remain unestablished.

name: ExpEvolve: Structuring and Reusing Experience for Open-Ended Discovery
summary: Extracts interpretable idea factors from archived programs whose score differences remain unexplained, then uses bandit-selected edits and plateau-triggered exploration to guide program evolution. Evaluations cover eleven mathematical tasks and six machine-learning engineering tasks. Reported gains concern bounded executable objectives; the theoretical benefits require stated assumptions, and transfer to expensive scientific verification remains untested.
status: The paper identifies itself as an extended version of CausalEvolve (arXiv:2603.14575). An official implementation release was not established from the inspected sources.

name: GAV: A scientific experimentation environment for PDE agents
summary: Learns continuous reference solutions and constructs matching PDE problems through manufactured solutions, giving coding agents numerical feedback without solving every new reference problem. Evaluations cover Navier–Stokes and Vlasov–Poisson-type tasks and adaptations of existing PDE agents. Its reliability analysis assumes controlled distribution mismatch and independent evaluation data; success on generated problems does not establish accuracy across arbitrary physical regimes.

name: Magnolia: A Persistent-Memory Agent Framework for Computational Chemistry
summary: Combines computational chemistry tools with session records, confirmed project knowledge, and human-reviewed rules reused across projects. Four case studies and controlled replays of four internal tasks examine the contribution of retained context. The authors explicitly position it as supervised research assistance; campaign-wide memory benefits remain unisolated, and complete docking records include unreleased collaborator results.

name: Autonomous adaptive spectral analysis with an LLM agent for self-driving laboratories
summary: Uses an LLM to inspect spectra and diagnostics, adjust predefined fitting parameters within bounded retries, or abstain, while deterministic code calculates the physical quantity. On 203 archived film spectra, it retains 183 baseline values, recovers 16 failed analyses, and abstains on four. This retrospective, single-campaign study does not test live laboratory control or detection of physically incorrect results that pass numerical checks.
status: Linked code belongs to the earlier deterministic optical-analysis campaign. Agent instructions are in this paper’s supplementary information; a standalone release of the complete agent workflow was not established.

name: Bayesian Model Discovery with Language Models: Closing the Loop between Hypotheses and Experiments
summary: Combines LLM-proposed functional forms with numerical parameter fitting, evidence-weighted predictions, and experiment selection by joint information gain over models and parameters. Four benchmarks compare predictive error and structural recovery, with ablations of numerical feedback. Results depend on the candidate pool, priors, and observation model; containing the true law as a special case is explicitly distinguished from recovering its exact form.
status: Preprint v1 inspected. No official implementation release was established from the examined primary sources.

name: Agentic AI–Physicist Collaboration in Experimental Particle Physics: A Proof-of-Concept Measurement with LEP Open Data
summary: Demonstrates an agent-assisted thrust analysis of archived ALEPH data, using supplied prior analyses, code execution, unfolding and manuscript drafting. Physicists define acceptance criteria, inspect outputs and approve scientific decisions. This is a supervised demonstration of a known observable, with no controlled productivity comparison; the paper’s descriptions of response-Monte-Carlo covariance and total uncertainty combination remain internally inconsistent.
status: Published in Highlights of High-Energy Physics, volume 2, issue 3, article 10, on 30 September 2026. The first preprint appeared on 5 March; v3 incorporates journal proofreading corrections.

name: OpenScientist: evaluating an open agentic AI co-scientist to accelerate biomedical discovery
summary: Evaluates an open hypothesis-testing agent on four featured biomedical case studies and three supplementary cases, combining data analysis, literature retrieval, and reports. Expert review identifies useful results alongside preprocessing mistakes, statistical weaknesses, and incomplete rejection on randomized controls. Selected cases and human prompt/data refinement limit generalization; estimated time savings are not a controlled productivity comparison.
status: medRxiv v1 was posted on 18 March 2026, as confirmed by the publisher metadata API; the DOI date fragment is not the posting date. Full text was read through Europe PMC. No independent reproduction was performed.

name: LitPivot: Developing Well-Situated Research Ideas Through Dynamic Contextualization and Critique within the Literature Landscape
summary: Links proposal editing to changing literature: researchers select problem, contribution, or evaluation facets, inspect relevant paper clusters, and consider excerpt-backed critiques and revisions. A 17-participant study reports stronger expert-rated literature grounding, with a five-participant qualitative follow-up. Novelty benefits are self-reported; short HCI/NLP ideation tasks do not establish feasibility, successful experiments, or long-term research impact.
status: UIST 2026 proceedings identity verified from ACM-deposited DOI metadata, matching the author manuscript. The current author version was read, but the publisher PDF and separately promised study-protocol supplement remain unavailable. Prototype source or access was not established.

name: PaperScorer: How Predictable Is Paper Acceptance?
summary: Trains text and vision models to predict acceptance from anonymized manuscripts, with stronger matched-source results from page images. ICLR inputs include rebuttal-era revisions, while arXiv rejection labels are inferred from missing proceedings matches. Accuracy concentrates at rating extremes and degrades across sources. The score estimates review outcomes; it does not establish correctness, novelty, or scientific impact.
status: The authors report NeurIPS 2026 acceptance. A proceedings record was not independently verified, so this entry retains the preprint source label. Results were inspected, not reproduced.

name: POSEIDON: Scaling Training Environments for Scientific Agents from Code Repositories
summary: Turns scientific repositories into reproduction, subflow, completion, and correction tasks using executable seed programs and iterative validation. The resulting Pearl collection supports supervised agent training, evaluated on six benchmark suites. A separate 600-environment human audit examines quality. Reported transfer depends on repository selection, generated evaluators, and benchmark exclusions; sample auditing does not certify every environment or establish autonomous scientific discovery.
status: The paper reports 97,659 training environments from 7,110 repositories, with intentional biological oversampling. An official implementation or Pearl download release was not established from the examined sources.

name: Do AI Scientists Know What's New?
summary: Audits proposal-level novelty checks and introduces ClaimNov, which extracts contribution claims, retrieves comparable prior claims, and produces evidence-linked novelty judgments. Tests distinguish disguised papers, disputed contributions, later-realized ideas, and mixed proposals. Results depend on fixed reference pools, heuristic novelty labels, and LLM generation and judging; they do not establish open-literature search completeness or better completed research.

name: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
summary: Introduces LongChang, where agents choose investigations and construct apparatus in simulated worlds with altered physical laws. Separate agents generate scenes and judge reports against hidden laws and exploration records. Evaluation distinguishes law correctness from experimental support and compares guidance, turn budgets, and apparatus access. Findings concern fixed simulated scenes and model-based judgments, not discovery of unknown real-world laws or independently validated scientific results.
status: The author-linked repository snapshot bfad4c7e63d3 contains a README and presentation assets, but no experiment source files despite documented run commands. Public implementation availability remains unverified.

name: AutoSciBench: Autonomous Benchmark Generation for Evaluating Scientific Agents
summary: Constructs scientific-agent tasks from high-level concepts and executable recipes, then revises them using solver trajectories and judge feedback. Experience from earlier refinements guides later generation across computational biology, materials science, and clinical imaging. The generator also serves as solver during refinement, and quality ratings come from LLM judges. Increased difficulty and favorable ratings do not independently establish scientific validity or broad evaluation coverage.
status: The paper describes generated tasks and evaluation procedures. A public implementation or downloadable task release was not established from the inspected primary sources.

name: MUSE: Multi-Level Memory with Selective Runtime Injection for Scientific Coding Agents
summary: Extracts global checks, problem-level approaches, and implementation lessons from completed coding attempts, then selectively injects relevant experience and review advice during execution. Comparisons span numerical solvers, GPU kernels, and scientific software repair. Memory banks are frozen before evaluation; transfer is tested between two kernel benchmarks using one agent and model family. Reported coding gains do not establish continual learning or end-to-end scientific discovery.

name: Collaborative AI agents for autonomous experimental research with solid-state quantum spins
summary: Coordinates question selection, theoretical derivation, computational checks, and nitrogen-vacancy spin experiments through agents that can reject or revise collaborators’ work. An acquisition agreeing with predictions was classified inconclusive after drift controls failed; a revised protocol passed retained criteria on four withheld targets. One configured laboratory and human-built apparatus bound the evidence. The public Auctopus engine excludes study prompts and instrument descriptions; experimental data and analysis code are request-only.
status: Auctopus 1.0.0 releases the agent engine and templates, while excluding the study prompts and instrument description. Its mock demo does not reproduce the paper; experimental data and analysis code remain request-only.

name: VerifiedLab: Harnessing Knowns for Unknowns
summary: Extracts perovskite-device records under versioned annotation and equivalence rules, calibrates verifiers against experts, and attaches category-level reliability to the database. Retrospective prediction uses a held-out publication year. The multi-agent discovery dialogue is illustrative, with selected held-out recipes, rather than a validated discovery experiment. Deployment reliability remains model-judged, and category accuracy does not establish confidence in individual values.
status: Paper, implementation tree, and README inspected at bafe1a7f2808 without execution. The paper links a data release; no dataset or model artifact was downloaded.

name: Beyond fabrication: Misattributed numbers in papers written by AI research agents
summary: Reanalyzes numerical claims in agent-written papers and distinguishes values unsupported by the recorded experiment from values absent from available artifacts. A deterministic context-and-decoy checker achieves high precision but limited recall on a small held-out human-labeled sample. Most uncertified claims remain traceable. Shared retrieval candidates, annotation revisions, incomplete large-run coverage, and changes to both judge model and harness constrain the conclusions.
status: Annotation follows v2, revised 31 October; date records the first submission. The study covers one benchmark and available released artifacts. A manuscript journal heading was not treated as a verified publication record.

name: ScienceCUA: Resource-to-Skill Construction and Execution-Guided Skill Evolution for Scientific Computer Use Agents
summary: Builds procedural skills and reference catalogs from scientific-software documentation, then revises them using execution failures and fresh-session validation. ScienceBoard-VE separates 108 evolution tasks from 168 repaired test tasks. Gains demonstrate transfer across related operations in six applications; a stronger model gains only 2.11 percentage points. Resource coverage, information volume, and routing differ across baselines, limiting claims about knowledge organization alone.
status: The pinned release includes Resource-to-Skill construction. Its README lists execution-guided skill self-evolution and benchmark components as planned future releases. Repository and paper were inspected without installation or execution.

name: Can LLM Agents Improve Imperfect Earth System Model Parameterizations?
summary: Compares expert-guided and unattended agents for translating and designing warm-rain parameterizations in JAX. Most gains concern executable, differentiable, mass-conserving closures; only two of 100 four-round candidates beat the best retuned physical baseline on rain-mass error. Expert-guided neural-ODE development required 131 prompts and remained less accurate. Missing source equations affect one translation test; box-model results do not establish coupled-climate performance.
status: Reviewed v1, sections 3–5 and Appendices F/I. The checklist describes a workshop submission and defers code release to a later journal version; no published venue record or public implementation was established.

name: Cloudra: Geometric Reasoning and Scientific Validation for Autonomous Reaction Mechanism Exploration
summary: Connects chemical species and reaction steps to geometric operations, quantum-chemical calculations, and explicit physical checks. Same-backbone comparisons on 50 mechanism tasks favour guided workflows, particularly in pathway support. Published scores use human reconstruction of run artifacts; full self-consistency concerns delivered objects rather than all requested steps. Electronic-energy agreement, computation cost, incomplete pathways, and method-limited negative conclusions require separate interpretation.
status: Inspected the paper-described 70daa5a source tree and README, plus current documentation at 005e9642cead. The current Standard mode differs from the paper baseline. No installation, calculation, or archive download was performed.

name: From AutoResearch to Continual AutoResearch: Do Agents Learn Across Tasks?
summary: Compares persistent and reset research agents on matched streams across nine ML task families. Persistent state improves early search efficiency, largely through faster or stronger initialization; only one agent shows a substantial aggregate final-performance gain. Matched insight cards do not consistently beat shuffled cards. Short fixed streams, mostly single paired runs, and bundled code–context retention limit claims about scientific learning across tasks.
status: Reviewed v1, sections 3–6 and memory/failure appendices. Models remain fixed; streams contain three to five tasks, usually with 30-minute budgets. The reproducibility statement schedules code release for a camera-ready version; public benchmark code was not established.

name: Verifier strength does not buy discovery quality: a pre-registered two-domain test of LLM-based automated research, with post-hoc evidence pointing to proposer-pool composition
summary: Re-gates fixed LLM and random proposal pools through three verifier tiers in scheduling and simulated edge offloading. Under author-reported frozen criteria, stricter filtering does not produce the predicted held-out ordering. Weak and standard gates usually select identical candidates. Exploratory pool merging helps only scheduling and also doubles proposal count. One 0.5B proposer, overlapping source instances, weak tier separation, and an unreachable strict-order criterion limit generalization.
status: Reviewed v1, sections 3–7. The linked Zenodo artifact record is restricted and exposes no public files; its protocols and ledgers were not independently audited. The manuscript’s journal-template heading was not treated as a publication record.

name: Are LLM Research Agents Reliable Judges of Predictability? Evidence from Planted-Signal Worlds
summary: Tests forecasting agents in simulated worlds with known predictive structure, separating their verdicts from sealed-holdout performance. Initial bootstrap worlds contain an exploitable repeated-value artifact; Gaussian-shock follow-ups still show frequent unsupported predictability claims and framing sensitivity. At matched false-positive rates, agents do not outperform conventional tests consistently. The brief leaves the decision threshold unspecified, and stronger baseline comparisons are exploratory.
status: Reviewed v1, study design, Gaussian-shock controls, discussion, and availability statement. Pre-specifications use tagged repository commits rather than a public registry. The replication package is described as planned for public deposit and available by request; no public implementation was verified.

name: Goal-Driven Autonomous Optical Experimentation via a Self-Recursive Hardware-Software Harness
summary: Demonstrates revised display-control software, spectral feedback, and response-model refinement in one optical see-through color-matching setup. An acknowledged RGB-hold interface passes 12 live control checks. Feedback improves five targets; a separate model revision helps seven of nine paired contexts, with two regressions. The error bound assumes uniform model accuracy and global optimization, neither established by sampled prediction scores; cross-goal transfer and general hardware redesign remain untested.
status: Reviewed v1 sections 4–7 and the source tree/README at 255a2f896040. The release covers device-control and acquisition software, not verified end-to-end research-agent orchestration. Observed measurements, fitted models, calibration, and vendor SDKs are excluded. No software or hardware was executed here.

name: CLEAR: Structured Specifications for Controllable Long-Horizon ML Research Engineering
summary: Converts papers and task descriptions into structured execution specifications, then uses a planner, coding workers, and localized repairs to construct ML pipelines. Evaluation covers PaperBench and MLE-Bench Lite; a matched-backbone specification ablation supports the intermediate representation. Other comparisons change model backbones as well as orchestration, limiting causal claims about heterogeneous routing. The optional human specification checkpoint was not used in reported runs.

name: DefectSkills: Guiding AI agents through first-principles calculations for point defects in semiconductors and insulators
summary: Packages expert defect-calculation protocols as reusable prompts for VASP setup, convergence checks, finite-size corrections, formation energies, and thermodynamic analysis. A BaCd2P2 demonstration covers seven defect species but requires researcher intervention on restart diagnosis, directory mapping, and substitution of a custom solver. The run informed prompt refinement; it does not establish held-out reliability or detailed defect-physics validation. Reference scripts and calculation data are linked.

name: A semi-autonomous multi-agent pipeline for high-energy astrophysics research with enforced provenance and verifiable self-extension
summary: Builds reusable astronomy tools behind deterministic checks and cross-model review, while requiring reported numbers to occur in recorded outputs or carry paper locators. On a planted-defect benchmark, the combined checks stop 64 of 65 defects but reject 40 of 69 correct controls. IXPE studies include qualified reproduction and null results. Provenance does not ensure scientific correctness; statistical and source-mixing errors survive the checks.

name: PharmAgents2: Towards Autonomous End-to-End Drug Discovery
summary: Combines paper-derived skills and parallel hypothesis investigations to deliver drug-discovery candidates. Evaluations cover 121 decision questions, three LLM-graded process tasks, and three selected studies followed by human assays. LpxH activity/binding and cytokine-signaling inhibition do not confirm the proposed binding site, covalency, or JAK1 selectivity. An anonymized target study and differing tool/skill access limit scrutiny and component attribution; learning from experimental outcomes remains future work.

name: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
summary: Accelerates evolutionary program search with batched latent agents, KV-cache communication, and hidden-state diversity filtering. Across 21 numerical tasks it evaluates more programs per hour than three text-based frameworks. Ablations show early search benefits, while zero-agent variants approach similar final scores. Improvements over historical AlphaEvolve constructions do not establish new global records, and fixed numerical evaluations provide limited evidence of broader scientific generalization.

name: Adaptive Experimentation Can Hide Model Error: Detection Limits and Falsification Budget
summary: Bounds model-adequacy detection in stationary, finite-action/outcome settings using the experimenter’s sampling distribution. Separates absent acquisition evidence from a detector’s failure to capture available signal. An expansion-relative diagnostic motivates reserving actions for falsification. Empirical evidence is mixed: the primary comparison fails detection eligibility, revisions depend on horizon, and measured-data replay retains fit-derived labels. Small selected LLM pilots and incomplete campaigns do not establish general scientific-reasoning gains.

name: Agentic intelligent data engine for scientific large language models
summary: Coordinates dataset discovery, quality screening, and code-based transformation for scientific RAG and instruction tuning. Biomedical and chemistry benchmarks support useful corpus construction, with smaller gains for chemistry retrieval than fine-tuning. Efficiency comparisons use measured pipeline runtime against expert time estimates. Reported overlap controls reduce contamination risk, while derived sources, dataset-level quality judgments, and corpus composition limit claims of verified scientific knowledge or autonomous discovery.

name: NORA: A Harness-Engineered Autonomous Research Agent for End-to-End Spatial Data Science
summary: Orchestrates spatial research through domain skills, persistent files, separate reviewers, and human checkpoints. Three case studies demonstrate useful workflow assistance while recording substantial expert intervention and lower human ratings of rigor than LLM ratings. Ablations are qualitative. Generated reports retain unresolved validation issues, including an invalid fairness-bound argument and uncalibrated elevation uncertainty, so workflow completion should not be treated as verified scientific discovery.

name: Brilliance for adaptive computational research in accelerator physics
summary: Combines reusable physics modules, agent-written programs, and JuTrack calculations to revise accelerator investigations. Cases include ideal storage-ring design and offline calibration against measured responses with a specialist reference. Detailed requests and further scientist guidance supply expertise. The sub-10-pm candidate retains momentum-acceptance limitations; finite tracking and single configuration comparisons do not establish operational readiness. Calibration agreement is not unique recovery of machine errors or residuals at measurement resolution.
status: Reviewed v3, revised 4 November 2026; the catalog date retains the original 11 October submission. Numerical research cases and offline calibration are distinct from commissioning or operating an accelerator.

name: Towards AI-Agent-Accelerated Research in High-Energy Physics: A Case Study in Monte Carlo Analysis
summary: Studies agent-assisted reconstruction and extension of a CEPC Bell-observable analysis through simulation, frozen definitions, deterministic checks, and diagnostic controls. Humans authorize state-changing work and retain scientific interpretation. The benchmark uses instructions rather than an information-access barrier, and the enlarged sample reuses development seeds. Four correlated selections are not independent replications. Active human time was not prospectively recorded, so no measured productivity speed-up is established.
